definition: In machine learning, the kernel perceptron is a variant of the popular perceptron learning algorithm that can learn kernel machines, i.e.
details: non-linear classifiers that employ a kernel function to compute the similarity of unseen samples to training samples. The algorithm was invented in 1964, making it the first kernel classification learner.

explainer.lead: The kernel perceptron is a variant of the perceptron learning algorithm that learns kernel machines, nonlinear classifiers using a kernel function to compare unseen samples with training samples. It was invented in 1964 and is the first kernel classification learner.

tiers.eli5: To classify something new, you compare it with examples you have already seen and weigh how similar it is to each; mistakes update the weights on those examples.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers use it as a simple online nonlinear classifier by keeping training samples as support; a pitfall is that the model grows with the number of training examples and needs efficient similarity computation.
tiers.paperLevel: A variant of the perceptron learning algorithm that learns kernel machines, i.e. nonlinear classifiers employing a kernel function to compute similarity of unseen samples to training samples.

explainer.example: A new sample is classified by summing kernel-similarity-weighted votes from stored training samples, with misclassifications adjusting the weights.
